title: tenant-fencing-claim-exporter-and-residency-audit-channel
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a tenant-level fencing claim exporter that emits verifiable daily snapshots describing dedicated capacity residency, network boundary assignments, retention policies actually applied, and active isolation controls. The exporter should produce signed bundles consumable by auditors and the Console's evidence viewer. This ticket covers schema design, signer/key management integration, export worker, per-tenant retention trace, API for on-demand snapshot generation, and a scheduled pipeline to push artifacts to S3 and to the Compliance UI. The goal is to provide a deterministic, auditable artifact for each dedicated tenant so customers can prove their data stayed within agreed geography and isolation settings.
acceptance_criteria:
- Daily snapshot for a tenant is produced and contains: node list with zones, instance IDs, container image digests, applied retention policy version, and active ACLs.
- Snapshot bundles are cryptographically signed using the platform key and verifiable via the public signer service.
- Console can fetch and render bundle metadata and provide download links.
- Export respects tenant retention settings (redaction / TTL) and does not expose token contents or PII.
- API endpoint /v1/tenants/:id/residency_snapshot returns last-snapshot metadata with ETag and can trigger on-demand generation.
- End-to-end tests cover generation, signing, storage, and Console rendering.
tasks: Design snapshot schema and canonical ordering (design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1q2TenantFenceSchema)
Integrate with KMS for signing (use dedicated key ring) and document key rotation procedure
Implement export worker to gather tenant topology and retention metadata
Add on-demand API endpoint and background job to queue generation jobs
Implement storage writer to S3 bucket with per-tenant prefix and lifecycle settings
Console: evidence viewer integration to list snapshots and verify signatures
Add e2e tests and property tests for schema determinism
Add telemetry: generation latency, bundle size, success/failure rates
design_decisions: Canonical JSON with deterministic key ordering chosen to avoid signature instability
Bundles will contain metadata + compressed NDJSON for entries to keep streaming validation simple
Use existing KMS integration rather than introducing new HSM; plan key-escrow for enterprise Private deploys
Redaction: any fields tagged PII are replaced with deterministic hashes; retention applied before signing
risks: Large tenants can produce very large bundles; may impact worker memory and S3 costs
Key compromise area: need rotation and revocation to be surfaced to auditors
Edge cases for on-prem/private where KMS integration differs (require installation notes)
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal tenant + 2 pilot customers in a staging Dedicated cluster
Beta: enable for all Dedicated tenants behind a feature flag and opt-in UI in Console
GA: default nightly snapshots for Dedicated paying customers and docs for auditors
notes: We should align on retention redaction guidance with Legal before GA. Also coordinate with Infra about IAM roles used by the exporter to read cluster topology and secrets manager access.
